nodes.title: Workspace module: team and roles, invites, API keys, brand, knowledge ingest with approval, offerings, integrations, signed webhooks, activity, undo, global search, share links. 35 tools, 3 routes.

The kernel registry writes an approved A2 action's args and result as plain JSON into action.args and action.result, which GET /v1/actions returns to every member. Any secret passed to, or returned by, an approval-gated tool is therefore stored and shown in clear.
nodes.mitigation: Workspace never puts a secret in args or result: credentials are staged encrypted first (integration.stage_secrets, then connect takes only the stash id), and new tokens (API key, invite, webhook signing secret, share link) are held encrypted and read once by the approving person (secret.reveal). Tests check action.args and action.result for the secret strings. Other modules must follow the same rule or the kernel should redact.

nodes.title: A secret created by an approved action (API key, invite token, webhook signing secret, share link) is not returned in the receipt. The result carries a revealId; the approving person reads the secret once with secret.reveal within 15 minutes; the held copy is AES-256-GCM encrypted and deleted on first read.
nodes.rationale: The kernel stores approved results in action.result in clear (risk.2026-10-21.kernel-stores-approval-args-and-results-in-clear), which breaks 'shown once'. The cost is one extra call, and a short-lived encrypted copy before the first read, so 'only the hash is stored' holds after reveal.
nodes.reverse_if: The kernel adds a way for a tool to return a value that is not persisted in action.result (for example a result redaction hook), or approvals stop persisting results; then return the token in the receipt and delete secret.reveal.

nodes.title: POST /v1/uploads/knowledge takes JSON ({filename, contentBase64} or {text}) and calls the knowledge.ingest tool, so files are limited to about 700 KB by the kernel's 1 MB body limit.
nodes.rationale: The kernel router decodes every body as UTF-8 text and caps it at 1 MB, which corrupts binary uploads; the module may not edit the kernel. One code path through the tool keeps roles and audit.
nodes.reverse_if: The kernel router passes raw bodies to a route (multipart or octet-stream); then accept real file uploads up to the 9 MB tool limit.

events.details: Workspace module built with 20 tests passing on a throwaway Postgres 16 (run twice, files in parallel). Not verified: real browser or phone use, large PDFs, hostile files, webhook DNS-rebinding, multi-process delivery.
